title: Editor WYSIWYG Gate Definition
stopConditions: Project Control cannot identify the Work path, owner repository, Checklist target, or Evidence target before editing.
WYSIWYG remains ambiguous or inherits a general Word/Google Docs/editor-framework meaning instead of a FlowDoc-specific definition.
The bounded textarea active text-block island is treated as WYSIWYG instead of a controlled fallback authoring surface.
Contenteditable, DOM innerHTML document truth, ProseMirror, Slate, TipTap, or another rich editor engine becomes approved before a separate entry decision.
The slice changes visible Editor UI behavior or copy instead of only adding a gate definition and boundary decision.
Any WYSIWYG runtime starts before all entry prerequisites are recorded as approved.
The slice promotes product readiness, broad frontend readiness, Core truth, Backend truth, Editor truth, FlowDoc product truth, or map truth.
verificationTarget: Editor defines FlowDoc-specific WYSIWYG entry criteria, keeps the active text input path textarea-only, blocks contenteditable and common rich editor engines, and records that WYSIWYG work may start only after all explicit prerequisites are approved.
summary: Done: Editor merge commit 4f12a87b5f1e5e440fdf1bf1231450002657fba9 adds the bounded WYSIWYG gate definition. The spec defines FlowDoc WYSIWYG as managed document-surface authoring and preserves the accepted direction Hybrid Managed Cards + one Active Text-Block Island. The boundary decision records WYSIWYG behavior categories, non-WYSIWYG behaviors, required entry prerequisites, blocked DOM-editable bindings, and blocked rich editor engine package names or prefixes. The current bounded textarea active text-block island remains allowed and explicitly not WYSIWYG. This does not enable WYSIWYG behavior, contenteditable runtime, ProseMirror, Slate, TipTap, visible UI changes, broad frontend readiness, product truth, or map truth.
